subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or per-agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but current tests and docs intentionally support persistent `/exec` session defaults, so changing precedence is a security/product boundary decision rather than a safe mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Clamp stored session exec policy
options.body: Treat global or per-agent exec config as the maximum allowed policy for resumed channel sessions, clearing or clamping stored session fields that exceed it.

options.title: Keep persistence and document reset
options.body: Preserve existing per-session `/exec` behavior and document that operators must reset sessions or run a repair flow after tightening exec policy.

options.title: Ship an explicit reset path first
options.body: Add a doctor or operator reset flow for stored exec fields before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Clamp stored session exec policy
recommendation.body: Treat global or per-agent exec config as the maximum allowed policy for resumed channel sessions, clearing or clamping stored session fields that exceed it.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest history trail for the `/exec` session override contract and current precedence tests points to steipete.
